text: {"score":3,"justification":"Core numbers match the card (16.1% vs 2.3%, 7.53, z 2.03, 59% low-complexity, 3 of 4 documented 99215 below billed, 1 of 16 data-reviewed). The cited claims fit their sentences, and the next steps are concrete. But there are issues: an unsupported 'random sample of 30 charts came back complete' claim (the card gives no sampling info), the overpayment estimate and CI are not in the card, the headline 25% and 20 documented 99214/99215s (16+4) are derived but fine, and the headline's 5% peer rate is not shown on the card. There is also redundancy, and the sentence 'excess 99215s are mostly on healthy patients' overstates, since the 99215 share at each complexity level is only higher than all-provider share, and 11.6%/15.2% are rates, not proportions of excess. Missing-data flags are weak.","problems":["Unsupported statement 'A random sample of 30 charts came back complete' – the card says only 30 documented claims, with no sampling or completeness info; it may mislead about selection bias (6% documented)","Overpayment estimate $3,364 (CI $1,635–$5,093) not traceable to the card; unverifiable","Headline 5% peer rate and 8% comparison rate: the card gives 11.1% for 99215 and 4.8% for 99214 across all providers, so 8% and 5% are only derived and unclear","'Excess 99215s are mostly on healthy patients' misuses 11.6%/15.2%, which are provider 99215 shares by complexity group, not shares of the excess","Tiny documented base (4 documented 99215s) is not flagged as thin evidence; the 'leaning' is stated more strongly than the data allow","Examples cited for 0-condition claims omit the dx; C0035419 is listed with 0 conditions but the claim is in the low-complexity list, fine; no high-complexity counterexamples or supported claim (C0035274) mentioned","Does not flag that only 6.1% of claims have documentation"]}
